Title: Coordinated attacks: Thailand's southern insurgency flares
Article:
A surge in attacks across Thailand's south has put a spotlight on the low-level insurgency by Muslim separatists that has killed thousands of people in the last two decades.
Dozens of coordinated night-time attacks across the three southernmost provinces near Malaysia over the weekend injured three people and left government buildings and vehicles burned.
They were followed on Monday by an explosion at a convenience store.
These are the latest incidents of incendiary attacks in the long-running conflict in Thailand's far south.
How did it start?
The region concerned used to be part of the former Malay-Muslim Patani sultanate but was annexed in the early 1900s by Buddhist-majority Thailand – then Siam – following an agreement with colonial power Britain.
Concerns about cultural identity, political representation and economic development grew.
From the 1960s militants including the main rebel group Barisan Revolusi Nasional (BRN) began fighting for an independent Islamic nation.
The current unrest began in January 2004 when militants raided an army base in Narathiwat province, killing several soldiers and stealing weapons.
In October that year security forces opened fire on protesters outside a police station in the town of Tak Bai, in Narathiwat, killing seven.
Following the shooting 78 people suffocated after they were arrested and stacked on top of each other in the back of Thai military trucks – a deadly crackdown widely seen as a trigger for the southern unrest.
The "Tak Bai massacre" has long been an emblem of state impunity in the Muslim-majority south, and 20 years later murder charges against seven officials were dismissed when the statute of limitations expired.
Since 2004 around 7,000 people have been killed in the simmering conflict, according to monitor Deep South Watch.
Are the recent attacks unusual?
In July assailants killed five soldiers in a shooting and bomb attack at a checkpoint. Six civilians were wounded.
The Thai government warned at the time of a series of violent incidents in the past two to three months that it blamed on a "terrorist network seeking to instil fear among the public and target state officials."
Former Thai MP and human rights advocate Kannavee Suebsang told AFP there was "an increase in the coordination and visibility of the attacks this year."
But Matthew Wheeler, International Crisis Group's senior analyst for Southeast Asia, said it was "business as usual."
Dozens of people are killed every year, with fatalities peaking at more than 200 annually in 2005-2007, figures from the Uppsala Conflict Data Program showed.
Last Saturday night's attacks were "remarkable only in their scale", which attracted media attention, Wheeler said in an email.
"These kinds of attacks have taken place weekly, if not daily, for more than two decades," he said.
What is the goal?
The attacks were not claimed, but Wheeler said they were a demonstration of militants' capabilities and continued presence, despite massive deployment of Thai security forces.
Munira Mustaffa, a Malaysia-based counterterrorism and extremism expert, said they were "frustrated signalling" by insurgents intended to "get the government to return to the table."
Thailand first held peace talks with the BRN in 2013 under Malaysian mediation, with the latest round held in December.
But negotiations have stalled repeatedly.
Thailand's head negotiator, Thanat Suwannanon, told local media this week the attacks may be intended to gain the upper hand in the next round of talks.
Thanat, who is also National Intelligence Agency director, said insurgents were also testing the readiness of security forces.
"They focus on symbolic attacks like burning buildings and vehicles of local government offices," he said.
Where now?
Thailand has reinforced its military presence in the south and Malaysia has also boosted security on the border.
The Thai government is "using the security apparatus to solve the problem", the rights advocate Kannavee said.
"But in fact this is a political problem."
BRN has asked for self-governance and a power-sharing mechanism with Bangkok, but the Thai side has only offered a seat at the table of a southern development agency, security analyst Don Pathan said.
Participation of local people, including landowners and community representatives, in the peace dialogue was crucial to making the process productive, Kannavee added.
The Thai negotiator Thanat said talks were expected to be held in late October, after discussions scheduled for September were postponed following the soldiers' deaths.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chinese vacuum maker Dreame winds down carmaking project
Article:
BEIJING: Chinese vacuum cleaner maker Dreame is winding down its electric-vehicle venture, which it launched with considerable fanfare in August 2025 with the stated goal of building "the world's fastest car", according to Chinese media reports.
The reported wind-down represents a dramatic reversal for the venture, codenamed "Star Project", that Dreame had championed as a key expansion beyond home appliances, with plans to launch its first luxury EVs in 2027.
The venture's workforce peaked at nearly 1,000 employees but has since been reduced to a few dozen staff, mainly in finance, legal and human resources, who are handling matters such as supplier settlements and corporate deregistration, state-owned Economic Daily reported on Monday.
Senior executives have begun seeking opportunities elsewhere, while the project has seen waves of layoffs and resignations, leaving large sections of its offices vacant, business outlet Yicai reported over the weekend.
The abrupt change came only months after Star Project outlined plans in February for flagship showrooms across the Middle East, including in Iraq, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar.
Dreame did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
In a statement posted on Weibo on Tuesday, Dreame said it had adjusted some exploratory businesses as part of a broader strategic refocus and would integrate related technologies, research results and resources into its core operations.
Dreame added that it would concentrate on four core areas: smart homes, outdoor living, smart mobility and embodied AI, without specifically addressing reports that it was exiting vehicle development.
"At present, the company's core product R&D, production, sales, delivery and after-sales services are operating normally, and its domestic and overseas businesses are progressing according to plan," the company said.
Earlier this year, Dreame showcased its Nebula NEXT 01 sports coupe and NEXT 01X luxury SUV concept vehicles at the Beijing auto show.
The company also aired a 30-second Super Bowl ad promoting its automotive ambitions.
The commercial, which cost US$10 million, featured a vacuum cleaner, lawn mower and futuristic sports car transforming into robots before hurling a flaming ball.

Title: [UPDATED] RM15,000 bet behind Johor highway illegal race
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A RM15,000 bet was allegedly placed on the illegal motorcycle race that saw a group block part of the Second Link highway in Johor last Saturday.
Bukit Aman Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) director Datuk Seri Mohammed Hasbullah Ali said the amount was uncovered during police questioning of suspects arrested over the incident.
"Based on the suspects' statements, the illegal race involved a RM15,000 bet," he said when contacted today.
Earlier today, a suspected
illegal motorcycle racing "jockey"
was among three men arrested after they allegedly tried to flee a police operation at a condominium in Sentul.
The trio, aged between 20 and 40, were detained in the condominium's car park at about 1.30am.
The operation was conducted by the department's Intelligence and Operations Unit following investigations into a viral video showing an illegal motorcycle race along the Linkedua Highway in Johor.
The suspects allegedly tried to flee during the operation but were apprehended by police and taken to the Kulai Traffic Police Station to assist investigations.
On Aug 23,
eight men aged between 26 and 45
, including a motorsport influencer, were arrested and remanded following the circulation of a 33-second video showing the highway allegedly being blocked to allow two motorcyclists to race.
The incident drew widespread attention after the video went viral on social media.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PetDagang's bumper commercial gains unlikely to recur in 2H26
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Petronas Dagangan Bhd's (PetDagang) commercial margins are expected to moderate in the second half of 2026 (2H FY26) as earlier price-lag gains reverse, with Brent crude prices rising towards US$90 per barrel.
Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) said PetDagang had benefited from a temporary timing advantage from fuel price movements, but this effect is expected to taper off.
Conversely, it expects retail margins to recover in Q3 FY26, supported by inventory gains from higher average selling prices under the automatic pricing mechanism.
Motor gasoline volumes are also expected to remain resilient, supported by strong customer stickiness within the Setel ecosystem.
"Meanwhile, the government has assured sufficient fuel supply through end-2026, alleviating concerns over potential supply disruptions and supporting near-term operational stability," HLIB said in a note.
PetDagang posted earnings of RM387.2 million in Q2 FY26, bringing its 1H FY26 core net profit to RM677.6 million.
The first-half earnings accounted for 60.5 per cent of HLIB's full-year forecast and 58.8 per cent of consensus estimates.
"Despite the strong results, we regard this to be within expectations as the bumper contribution from the commercial segment is unlikely to recur in 2H FY26 if oil prices remain at the US$80 to US$90 per barrel range," it said.
HLIB maintained its "Buy" call on PetDagang with a target price of RM21.34.
In a separate note, RHB Research remained positive on PetDagang's medium-term earnings resilience, underpinned by its diversified earnings portfolio, supply-chain strength and growing Setel ecosystem.
It maintained its "Buy" call on the stock with a target price of RM22.37.
RHB said PetDagang's 1H FY26 core earnings came in above its expectations at 68 per cent of its full-year forecast, while meeting consensus expectations at 59 per cent.
"Despite the earnings beat, we maintain our earnings forecasts and target price of RM22.37 as the stronger-than-expected performance of the commercial segment was largely driven by favourable, timing-related price lag gains, which we expect to normalise in 2H FY26," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 38 held over suspected migrant smuggling via Sungai Kelantan
Article:
PASIR PUTEH: A Malaysian man suspected of being a migrant smuggler was arrested with 37 undocumented Myanmar nationals in Kampung Cina, Kota Bharu, yesterday.
Kelantan Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) director Maritime Captain Kamal Mohamad said the arrests were made following intelligence on migrant smuggling activities through an illegal route along Sungai Kelantan.
He said an MMEA patrol boat conducting an operation detected a speedboat moving suspiciously in the darkness near Kuala Besar around 5.20am.
"However, the boat escaped by speeding into a narrow and shallow river channel. The darkness also made it difficult for the MMEA patrol boat to reach the location.
"At the same time, the MMEA land operations team was deployed to the Sungai Kelantan embankment near Kampung Cina to intercept the group," he said.
Kamal said a subsequent search led to the arrest of 38 people, including the Malaysian man suspected of acting as a migrant smuggler or agent.
A motorcycle was also found with the group, he added.
He said the 37 Myanmar nationals comprised 25 men, 11 women, aged between 15 and 41, and a six-month-old baby boy.
"Seven had documents but could not produce valid travel records showing they had legally entered Malaysia, while 30 others failed to produce any identification documents," he said.
Kamal said a urine test on the Malaysian suspect was positive for methamphetamine.
He said the Malaysian suspect was being investigated under the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act (ATIPSOM) 2007 for suspected involvement in migrant smuggling.
The Myanmar nationals were being investigated under the Immigration Act 1959/63 for allegedly entering and remaining in Malaysia without valid documents and travel records.
All 38 suspects were taken to the Kelantan Maritime headquarters for further investigation.
Kamal said the arrest of the 38 individuals was the largest recorded by the Kelantan MMEA this year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China prepares for more heavy rain from back-to-back storms
Article:
HONG KONG: China's coastal areas and southern regions are preparing for days of intense precipitation, with tens of thousands of people evacuated as Typhoon Narra tracks inland and another storm churns toward the country's eastern seaboard.
Narra made landfall as a tropical storm on Tuesday evening in the southern island province of Hainan after lingering over the Beibu Gulf  — also known as the Gulf of Tonkin — for several days, dumping heavy rain across Guangxi, Hainan and Guangdong.
Narra and the accompanying Typhoon Saudel, alongside tropical cyclones Gaenari and Atsani, form a rare quartet of storms swirling simultaneously across the Northwest Pacific and South China Sea, according to China's Meteorological Administration.
The multi-storm system has forced regional authorities including in Guangxi and Hainan to close businesses, suspend tourist operations and evacuate tens of thousands of residents.
Heavy rain is expected to persist in the south, even as recent downpours have already pushed rivers over warning levels and inundated low-lying areas in Guangxi.
Typhoon Saudel is forecast to make landfall along China's eastern seaboard between Zhejiang and Fujian provinces between Thursday and Friday, with weather models projecting its outer rain bands could extend back toward Guangxi.
Saudel swept across Japan's Okinawa prefecture early on Wednesday, prompting weather agencies to issue warnings for destructive winds and high seas.
As the storm moved west, it brought the Amami island chain in Kagoshima Prefecture into its storm-force wind radius, leaving nearly 35,000 homes without power, according to Kyushu Electric.
A total of 92 flights serving airports across Okinawa Prefecture were cancelled on Wednesday, while All Nippon Airways suspended all flights to and from Naha Airport, the prefecture's main gateway, public broadcaster NHK reported.
Taiwan's Central Weather Administration said Saudel is tracking north of the island, where it is expected to gradually weaken and shrink in storm radius, bringing moderate rainfall to parts of northern and southern Taiwan through Friday.

Title: Elderly couple turn discarded bottles into National Month decor
Article:
JERTIH: From piles of used plastic water bottles collected around an oil palm plantation, an elderly couple in Kampung Baru Tok Dor here have created colourful flower decorations for National Month celebrations.
Their creativity has not only brightened the village but also showcased their patriotism while giving discarded materials a new lease of life.
Halimah Said, 65, said she and her husband, Mat Ail Mamat, 78, began making the decorations on Aug 1 for a house decoration competition held in conjunction with National Month celebrations at village level.
"This is our second year taking part. We came second last year and wanted to try something different this time by using recycled materials.
"I collected discarded water bottles from a nearby oil palm plantation before cleaning, cutting and shaping them into flower petals. We have made at least five types of flowers, which were painted and arranged around the house," she said when met at her home recently.
Halimah said she spent about RM100 on red, yellow, white and blue spray paint, while most of the materials were sourced from discarded items.
The flowers were placed in pots and arranged along the fence, while red-and-white painted bottles were hung alternately on wooden poles beneath the Jalur Gemilang.
"We also plan to decorate a trishaw at the front of the house and build a replica of the Kuala Lumpur Twin Towers (KLCC)," she said.
Flags from several states were also displayed, symbolising diversity and patriotism.
Halimah said the activity had also given her a meaningful pastime while caring for her daughter, Rosnani Mat Ail, 41, who has been bedridden since infancy due to a disability.
Her children, grandchildren, nieces and nephews also helped print colour photographs of all former prime ministers, together with related information, for the patriotic-themed decorations.
"My nephew, Muhammad Aiman Mat Jusoh, 23, who lives nearby, comes almost every day to help prepare the decorations.
"Through this, we can spend our time meaningfully while strengthening family ties," she said.
She said using discarded materials also allowed the family to express their creativity without spending much.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian man, girlfriend nabbed in Medan over drug-laced vapes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian man and his Indonesian girlfriend were arrested in Medan, Indonesia, last week for trafficking vape products laced with drugs.
The 22-year-old Malaysian and his 35-year-old partner were detained by police in a car at a parking lot in Deli Serdang, along with 29 vape pods containing liquid drugs.
According to an Antara News report, Medan police Narcotics Investigation chief Assistant Commissioner Rafli Yusuf Nugraha said police had been investigating drug distribution in the area.
"Upon searching the vehicle, we found 24 vape pods containing drugs inside a backpack," he told a press conference.
Rafli said a subsequent raid on the couple's rented home in Medan Petisah yielded five more drug-laced vape pods and RM15,000 in cash inside a safe.
"We believe the Malaysian suspect and the woman met on social media before meeting in Malaysia and agreeing to distribute drugs in Medan.
"Initial investigations showed the Malaysian suspect brought 20 drug-laced vape pods from Malaysia in July, which were all sold with the help of his girlfriend, primarily to her friends in Medan," he said.
Rafli said the suspect smuggled the items into Indonesia by concealing them between folded clothes inside his luggage.
He added that during a second trip, the suspect brought 40 drug-laced vape pods from Malaysia using the same modus operandi, with the 29 seized units believed to be the remainder of that batch.
Both suspects tested positive for drugs following urine tests.
Indonesian police are expanding their probe to trace the supply network and distribution routes in Medan, and will coordinate with their Malaysian counterparts to identify the mastermind in Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mamdani explains opposition to NYC event with leader of India's Hindu nationalist group
Article:
WASHINGTON: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said on Tuesday he did not support an upcoming event in his city featuring the leader of the Hindu nationalist group that is the ideological parent of India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Mohan Bhagwat, chief of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), is scheduled to speak at a Manhattan event on Saturday, according to the event's website.
"I don't support the rally, but I don't know if the city has any jurisdiction on cancelling a private event," Mamdani, who is the first Muslim and Indian American mayor of New York City, said when asked if the event should be cancelled.
"The vision of India that I was taught by my family and one that I grew up being very familiar with was of a pluralistic society of a secular Republic that believed in the belonging of each and every person who was from India.
"And it has been incredibly troubling to see the rise of a movement that is predicated on an exclusionary vision."
The event's website casts the Aug 29 gathering as the "Universal Oneness Celebration" bringing together the Hindu American community.
The organisers, American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue, say the event is backed by several Hindu American groups and promotes shared heritage and interfaith unity.
Many local organisations have criticised it over Bhagwat's attendance and the RSS' history.
The RSS, a powerful Hindu group from which Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's BJP emerged, said in May it had organised foreign visits, including to the US, to counter perceptions it is a paramilitary outfit involved in attacks on minority communities.
The US Commission on International Religious Freedom says the RSS "has been involved in acts of extreme violence and intolerance against members of minority groups for decades."
The RSS disputes intolerance accusations and says it is a "Hindu centric civilisational, cultural movement" whose goal is to "carry the nation to the pinnacle of glory," including by uniting Hindus.
United Nations and human rights groups say abuse of Indian minorities has risen in recent years, pointing to rising hate speeches, a religion-based citizenship law, the demolition of Muslim-owned properties, the removal of Muslim-majority Kashmir's autonomy and an anti-conversion legislation that challenges freedom of belief.
The BJP-led Indian government denies being discriminatory and says its policies, including food subsidy programmes and electrification drives, benefit all communities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three killed, three injured in Kunak crash
Article:
KUNAK: Three people were killed and three others injured after the car they were travelling in skidded and crashed at Km7 of Jalan Kunak-Semporna here yesterday.
District police chief Superintendent Rejali Ak Angong said the driver and two passengers were pronounced dead at the scene by Health Ministry medical personnel following the 6.03pm crash.
He said the Perodua Viva was travelling from Kalabakan to Kampung Sungai Langgas with six people on board, including the driver, two adults and three children.
"Upon reaching the location, the driver lost control of the vehicle, causing it to skid and crash," he said in a statement today.
Rejali said another passenger was seriously injured, while two others suffered minor injuries. All three were taken to Kunak Hospital for further treatment.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Rejali urged motorists to remain vigilant and exercise caution while driving.

Title: Malay unity should prioritise governance over electoral engineering
Article:
LETTER:
Musyawarah Nasional 2.0 demonstrated that Malay political cooperation has acquired a useful meeting place, but it did not establish a new political alignment.
The Aug 25 forum in Kuala Lumpur was centred on Tabung Haji governance, not a negotiation among Malay parties.
Its significance lies elsewhere: competing political figures could debate accountability without first agreeing on electoral partnership.
Musyawarah Nasional was conceived earlier this year as an inclusive platform for Malay-Muslim NGOs, professionals and opinion leaders, structured around religion, politics, economics, education and social affairs.
Umno President, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi proposed registering it as an independent NGO rather than allowing ownership by any party or individual. That institutional design matters.
A civic platform survives only if it can discuss interests without becoming another vehicle for electoral bargaining.
Yesterday provided meaningful evidence. Zahid attended alongside Umno leaders, while opposition parliamentarians were also present.
Discussion focused on the Tabung Haji Royal Commission of Inquiry and competing interpretations of its financial history.
Former Auditor-General Madinah Mohamad argued that differing audit methodologies explained contrasting financial assessments.
Asyraf Wajdi questioned the capacity of Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB) to meet obligations connected with transferred assets. Zahid supported further scrutiny, preferring a Public Accounts Committee mechanism for examining management after 2017.
Opposition voices reportedly favoured renewed RCI scrutiny. That disagreement deserves attention. Unity worthy of the name cannot mean everyone repeating identical slogans.
Mature Malay political and civil-society cooperation must accommodate disagreement while producing mechanisms for evidence and accountability.
Tabung Haji is an appropriate test because its depositors' interests transcend party boundaries.
Protecting Muslim savings should not require agreement on who deserves political credit.
Claims that Musyawarah Nasional has already united Umno, Pas, Bersatu, Wawasan and Malay NGOs outrun the evidence.
No verified agreement from yesterday established common candidates, seat allocations, leadership hierarchy or a governing programme.
Those are the hard currencies of political realignment. Photographs, speeches and cordial attendance create atmosphere; they do not transfer votes.
Recent developments make this conversation more consequential. Pas and Umno have periodically explored renewed cooperation, while proposals for seat accommodation before GE16 have circulated.
Meanwhile, tensions within PN, particularly involving Pas, Bersatu and Wawasan, demonstrate that Malay political consolidation is not mechanically achievable.
Leadership compatibility, organisational interests and constituency claims remain formidable obstacles.
History cautions. Muafakat Nasional once demonstrated that Umno-Pas cooperation could mobilise Malay-Muslim enthusiasm, yet strategic disagreements and changing national alliances eventually weakened it.
The lesson is straightforward: emotional unity can generate rallies, but institutional unity requires rules. Without agreed decision-making, dispute resolution, candidate selection and policy priorities, fraternity eventually encounters arithmetic.
For Zahid, Musyawarah Nasional allows Umno to become a convening centre without abandoning the Madani government.
For PKR President, Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, this need not threaten coalition stability if the platform strengthens socioeconomic policy and institutional accountability rather than becoming anti-PH mobilisation.
Pas may see opportunities for Malay cooperation; Wawasan may seek space as a bridge; Bersatu faces the harder task of protecting relevance while its relationships within PN remain contested.
Economics should discipline the politics. Malay advancement cannot be reduced to electoral engineering.
Income, education, skills, entrepreneurship, institutional integrity and ownership in future industries matter more than ceremonial unity declarations.
Any platform claiming to represent Malay interests should publish measurable programmes and outcomes rather than merely diagnose communal anxiety.
Non-Malay confidence matters equally. Malaysia's constitutional order recognises Malay and Bumiputera interests while operating within a multi-ethnic federation.
A Malay cooperation agenda that appears exclusionary would impose costs, weaken national cohesion and complicate investor perceptions.
The stronger proposition is therefore inclusive advancement: strengthen Malay socioeconomic capacity without converting policy objectives into communal confrontation.
Musyawarah Nasional has created momentum, but presently it is momentum for dialogue rather than proof of realignment.
Its credibility will depend on whether a permanent secretariat follows resolutions, publishes progress, welcomes competing evidence and remains independent of partisan ownership.
The GE16 test is simple. If Umno, Pas, Wawasan, Bersatu and civil-society organisations can cooperate on institutional reform, socioeconomic programmes and evidence-based policy while managing electoral differences transparently, Musyawarah Nasional could become consequential.
If it becomes another stage for personalities and slogans, Malaysia has seen that performance before.
Malay unity becomes valuable only when it produces better governance, prosperity and stronger institutions for every Malaysian.
AZAM DATO MOHD
Political, economic analyst
Kuala Lumpur
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Inquest into Zara Qairina's death briefly halted after tense exchange
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Proceedings at the inquest into the death of 13-year-old Zara Qairina Mahathir were paused for more than 30 minutes after coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan left the courtroom following a tense exchange.
The exchange occurred during lawyer Datuk Ram Singh's questioning of consultant psychiatrist Dr Wong Haw Huo, the 75th witness in the inquest, over the manner in which Wong was responding to his questions.
Lawyer Datuk Ridzwandean Bukhary M. Borhan objected and raised concerns over what he described as "harsh" questions being put to the witness.
Ram told the court that other experts who had previously testified, including forensic pathologist Dr Bhupinder Singh, had been questioned in the same manner, before urging the court to be fair to them.
Ram: "Don't use the word 'harsh' on me. In the past, this is towards the end. There were very harsh also. I'm not here for that. But this is very important for us. Very important. Okay."
Amir Shah: "But this is an inquest, not a trial."
Ram: "I'm not saying it's a trial. He (the witness) is making it the way it is, uh, making us to cross him, but we are not crossing him. Tuan, I mean, let's be fair to us. Let's be fair. I don't see that there are any...."
Amir Shah: "Am I not fair enough?"
Ram: "You are fair, Tuan."
Amir Shah: "Am I not fair enough?"
Ram: "No, Tuan. Let's not get too agitated with this. He is going round and round and explaining. Okay?"
Amir Shah then left the courtroom without giving any instructions or indicating that the proceedings were to stand down.
Earlier, Ram had repeatedly asked Wong to provide direct answers to his questions, including on the cause of Zara Qairina's fall and whether the teenager was alone before the incident.
Proceedings resumed at 10.50am, with Ram and Ridzwandean apologising to the court.
Ram: "As a senior lawyer, it is not meant as what maybe Your Honour might think or the audience in this court. All I ask the witness to do is to answer questions directly. So, I tender my sincere apologies, first of all, to Tuan. I know we are towards the end of the inquest. It is not done yet."
Coroner: "Did you in any way insinuate that the bench is not being fair to you?"
Ram: "No, don't use the word 'insinuate'. I have not the slightest indication or slightest thought in my mind on that issue. All I said was let us all be fair. Of course, I did not want to ignore that too, but by saying him, I want to proceed. Of course, it came as a shock to me as a counsel in this inquest that Tuan got up just now. I hope this thing will not happen again."
Ridzwandean: "I would also like to tender my apologies if my talk was a bit excessive and I have objected to the question. So, I tender my sincerest apologies."
The coroner also apologised to those in the courtroom, saying it was the first time in his 21 years on the bench that he had "burst out" and left the bench.
Coroner: "It is me who apologise to you all because this is the first time in my entire 21 years on the bench that I have burst out. This is the first time, and this is also the first time that I have stepped down from the bench, and 'rasa sakit dada sikit' (felt a slight pain in my chest).
"Let's not be emotional. Let's be professional. That is the main aim of this inquest.
"Datuk Ram, I accept your apology as well as Ridzwandean's, but with caution. I remember I have given this reminder before, haven't I? We should conduct this inquest smoothly, fairly and professionally. It is important for the witness to answer and explain his answers because there is no cross-examination. As much as I can be fair to you, please be fair to me as well."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump raises prospect of demolishing iconic Kennedy Centre
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's administration suggested Tuesday that the Kennedy Centre in Washington could be demolished if courts block his plans to overhaul the performing arts landmark.
The extraordinary warning came in a Justice Department filing opposing efforts by Democrats to halt a two-year renovation and to prevent Trump's name being prominently added to the building.
The filing does not say there is a plan to demolish the complex. But it argues that without Trump's restoration and fundraising efforts, it would become increasingly hazardous to visit until it had to be torn down.
"Without those efforts, the centre will deteriorate further into an unsafe, decrepit structure that will be required to be taken down," Justice Department attorney Brantley Mayers wrote.
He suggested the site could then house a large outdoor amphitheater overlooking the Potomac River, acknowledging that this would "fail to adequately honor" slain president John F. Kennedy but would be cheaper to build and maintain.
The demolition warning marks an escalation in a bitter battle over one of the best-known cultural institutions in the United States.
The filing described the venue as "structurally unsound, fundamentally unsafe, and embarrassing to the nation's capital" and portrayed Trump as uniquely capable of rescuing it.
Justice Department lawyers said Trump's administration had secured $258 million from Congress for restoration and attracted a new donor base, arguing that recognition of the president was essential to keeping contributors on board.
Trump's handpicked Kennedy Center board recently voted to place the words "Restored and Renovated by President Donald J. Trump" beneath the institution's name and to rename its surrounding site the "President Donald J. Trump Plaza."
Congresswoman Joyce Beatty, an ex officio member of the board who brought the suit, has challenged Trump's efforts to put his name on the center, arguing that only Congress can name the institution established as a "living memorial" to Kennedy.
A federal judge previously agreed that the board could not simply rename the center and ordered earlier Trump signage removed. The administration is appealing.
Kennedy Centre officials had previously described the planned work in much less dramatic terms, saying it would involve extensive electrical, stage and leak-prevention repairs but would neither materially alter the exterior nor reduce the building to its structural frame.
A hearing on the proposed closure and latest effort to recognise Trump on the building is scheduled for Thursday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor Sultan urges leaders not to exploit differences to divide Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah has reminded leaders and politicians not to use political, racial or religious differences as an excuse to divide the people.
The Sultan said while flying thousands of Jalur Gemilang during National Month was an easy task, the greater challenge was building a nation where every citizen felt respected, accepted and proud to be Malaysian.
"Independence is not merely to be celebrated, and the flag is not merely to be flown.
"The true value of both lies in our ability to defend a nation where its people can live together in peace, mutual respect and unity.
"Leaders and politicians should set an example by practising moderation, tolerance and compassion, and not use political, racial or religious differences as an excuse to divide the people," he said in a statement issued by Istana Alam Shah today.
The Ruler said the Jalur Gemilang did not discriminate against Malays, Chinese, Indians, Kadazan-Dusuns, Ibans or any other ethnic group, nor did it differentiate between Muslims, Buddhists, Christians, Hindus or followers of other faiths.
He urged the younger generation to be taught to respect people from diverse religions, races and cultures.
"Although we differ in race, religion, language, political beliefs and backgrounds, the Jalur Gemilang reminds us that we remain citizens of the same nation.
"This flag belongs to all of us.
"We must take pride in it as it is a symbol of national unity," he added.
Sultan Sharafuddin said the spirit of National Day should also be reflected in honouring and appreciating the contributions of Malaysians who had dedicated their lives to uniting communities and bridging divides.
The Sultan also consented to the Jalur Gemilang being flown on the state flagpole at Dataran Selangor from Aug 26 to Sept 17.
A flag-raising ceremony was held today to mark the occasion and promote the spirit of patriotism and unity.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: ITMAX earnings seen setting new base as smart city rollout accelerates: HLIB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: ITMAX System Bhd's quarterly earnings of around RM30 million could become the new base for the coming quarters, supported by its smart parking and CCTV businesses, according to Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB).
Analyst Sam Jun Kit said the digital services infrastructure (DSI) segment also has room to grow in the second half of financial year 2026 (2H FY26), supported by the full contribution from MBJB smart parking, which started on May 1.
Unlike the first phase of its smart parking rollout, where ITMAX incurred upfront costs to reactivate parking bays, most of Johor Baru's 70,000 gazetted parking bays are already active.
He said the collection rate is also significantly higher at around 30 per cent, providing further growth potential for the company.
"Looking into FY27, earnings growth will be driven by the additional 2,000 CCTVs in MBJB, alongside the Kota Kinabalu City Hall (DBKK) CCTV and Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) projects.
"While the latter two will be recognised under the supply, installation and maintenance services (SINMS) segment, we understand their margins are broadly comparable to CCTV contracts," he said.
On ITMAX's second-quarter earnings, Sam said the company's core profit after tax and minority interest (Patami) of RM30.5 million, up 16.7 per cent year-on-year, brought first-half core Patami to RM55 million, up 27.3 per cent year-on-year.
He said the results were within both HLIB's and consensus expectations, accounting for 46 per cent and 45 per cent of their respective full-year forecasts, as stronger earnings are expected in 2H.
For the second quarter, revenue increased 13.9 per cent quarter-on-quarter, driven by stronger contributions from DSI and SINMS.
HLIB maintained its "Buy" call on ITMAX with an unchanged target price of RM6.08, based on a discounted cash flow valuation with a seven per cent weighted average cost of capital and three per cent terminal growth rate.
Sam said the terminal growth assumption reflected the long runway for CCTV deployment across Malaysia, supported by national digitalisation and smart city initiatives.
ITMAX's current rollout of 10,000 CCTV units for DBKL remains small compared with Singapore's 90,000 units, while Singapore is targeting 200,000 units by 2030.
"Over time, we also expect ITMAX to monetise its infrastructure further through smart city applications such as digital twins, traffic impact assessments and analytics, cementing its role as a key enabler of urban digital transformation," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Missing Kafa teacher found safe in Kedah
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A Kafa teacher who was reported missing from Sungai Ara on Sunday was found safe in Pokok Sena, Kedah, early today.
Mohamad Hijazi Zamri, 26, was
reported missing
on Aug 23 after leaving his home in Lilitan Sungai Ara at 8.40pm on a blue Yamaha LC135 motorcycle.
Southwest district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuwal Ab Wahab said police traced him to a house in Kampung Bukit Payong, Mukim Gajah Mati, Pokok Sena.
"Checks found that he was well and had no physical injuries," he said today.
Hijazi was taken to the Bayan Lepas police station for further action before being reunited with his family.
Anuwal thanked all parties who assisted in the search.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bersatu backs two Pahang reps' support for Wan Rosdy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu has taken note of two of its Pahang state assemblymen declaring support for Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail, party vice-president Datuk Seri Ahmad Faizal Azumu said.
"The Bersatu Political Bureau, chaired by party president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, discussed the matter from every angle and, in principle, supports the move," he said in a statement.
Kuala Sentul assemblyman Datuk Jasri Jamaluddin and Lepar assemblyman Mohd Yazid Mohd Yunus pledged their
support
for Wan Rosdy through a memorandum of understanding signed by the menteri besar and both assemblymen.
"Both assemblymen conveyed their wish to do so to the party leadership and left the decision to the party," he said.
He said the decision was made to safeguard political stability in Pahang and ensure the welfare of the people in both constituencies received proper attention from the state government.
Jasri and Yazid pledged to support Wan Rosdy's administration until the 16th state election.
BN and PN each hold 17 seats in the 42-member Pahang Legislative Assembly, with PN's 17 seats comprising 15 Pas assemblymen and the two Bersatu representatives, Jasri and Yazid.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Suspected 'jockey' among three nabbed after trying to flee police
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A suspected illegal motorcycle racing "jockey" was among three men arrested after they allegedly tried to flee a police operation at a condominium in Sentul.
Federal Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) director Datuk Seri Mohammed Hasbullah Ali said the trio, aged between 20 and 40, were arrested at the condominium's car park at about 1.30am.
He said the arrests were made by the department's Intelligence and Operations Unit following investigations into a viral video showing an illegal motorcycle race on the Second Link highway in Johor.
"The suspects are believed to have attempted to flee during the operation but were successfully apprehended by police.
"One of those arrested is believed to have been the motorcycle racer, or 'jockey', while the other two were spectators," he said in a statement today.
Hasbullah said the three were subsequently taken to the Kulai traffic police station in Johor to assist investigations.
The case is being investigated under Sections 42(1) and 81(2) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Police, he said, would continue taking stern action against those involved in illegal racing activities that could endanger other road users.
Earlier today, it was reported that the three were
arrested
in Kuala Lumpur.
The latest arrests bring to 11 the number of men detained in connection with the incident, which took place around 7am on Aug 22 along the highway between Km33 near the Senai toll exit and Km31 near the Johor Premium Outlet (JPO) interchange.
On Aug 23, eight men aged between 26 and 45, including a motorsport influencer were arrested and remanded following the circulation of a 33-second video clip showing the highway allegedly being blocked to clear the way for two motorcyclists to race.
The incident drew attention after the video went
viral
on social media.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump orders US flags lowered for 'true loss' of Dolly Parton
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump on Wednesday ordered flags across the United States to be flown at half-mast for a week in honour of Dolly Parton, calling the country music legend's death a "true loss for millions of people".
"Very sad to report that Dolly Parton, one of the greatest Country singers, and far beyond, EVER, has just passed away," Trump posted on his Truth Social network. "There has never been anyone like her, and never will," he said.
Americans from all walks of life united
in grief
on Tuesday over the death of country music legend Dolly Parton, praising her music, philanthropy and film work.
The singer, who died aged 80, was long regarded as one of the few celebrities loved by almost everyone. True to form, she was mourned by figures across the entertainment world, as well as politicians from both sides of the aisle.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Myanmar man charged with sexually assaulting 3-year-old Australian
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A Myanmar hotel worker was charged in the Sessions Court here today with sexually assaulting a three-year-old Australian boy at a stall last week.
Aung Phyo Win, 30, claimed trial after the charge was read to him in Bahasa Melayu before Sessions Court Judge Juraidah Abbas.
According to the charge, Aung Phyo is alleged to have sexually assaulted the child by touching him inappropriately.
He allegedly committed the offence at Warung Penjaja, Lorong Baharu, at about 9.10pm on Aug 20.
The charge was framed under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, which carries a maximum 20-year jail term and whipping upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Anuarul Hakim Abdul Muen prosecuted, while lawyer K. Mahendran represented Aung Phyo.
Earlier, Judge Juraidah asked Aung Phyo whether he could fully understand Bahasa Melayu.
The accused told the court that he had been working in Malaysia for four years and was married.
During the proceedings, Mahendran applied for bail, saying two Malaysians were prepared to stand as sureties.
He also said his client would comply with any additional conditions imposed by the court and that his passport had been handed over to police.
However, Anuarul objected to bail, saying the prosecution had yet to receive confirmation on the authenticity of the accused's passport.
"Although the accused's passport has been handed over to the police, the court has yet to receive documents confirming its validity. Therefore, the prosecution requests that bail not be granted," he said.
The court denied bail and fixed Sept 28 for mention of the case and submission of documents.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd
