Title: KLK gets mixed calls as analysts weigh earnings recovery against valuation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK) has received mixed calls from analysts following its latest quarterly results.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) research downgraded the stock to "Hold" from the "Buy" call, while CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd maintained its "Buy" recommendation.
HLIB analyst Chye Wen Fei said KLK's core earnings of RM911.2 million in the first nine months of financial year 2026 (9M FY26) were within expectations, supported by an anticipated stronger performance from its plantation and manufacturing segments in the final quarter.
The investment bank raised its target price to RM22.72 from RM21.97 after lifting its FY26 to FY28 core earnings forecasts by 1.8 per cent, 1.8 per cent and 4.7 per cent, respectively, mainly on higher crude palm oil (CPO) price assumptions.
However, its downgrade on KLK to "Hold" from "Buy" is because of less attractive valuations following the stock's recent share price run-up.
CIMB Securities analyst Ivy Ng Lee Fang raised KLK's target price to RM24.32 from RM23.70.
She said KLK's third-quarter (Q3) core net profit fell 25 per cent year-on-year and 16 per cent quarter-on-quarter to RM254 million, mainly due to higher associate losses.
Its 9M FY26 core net profit of RM891 million, down 11 per cent year-on-year, accounted for 70 per cent of CIMB Securities' FY26 forecast and was broadly in line with expectations, although it represented only 66 per cent of consensus.
Ng said underlying operations improved, with plantation and manufacturing earnings before interest and tax (Ebit) both rising year-on-year in Q3 FY26.
"We expect stronger Q4 FY26 core earnings on firmer CPO prices, improving fresh fruit bunches (FFB) output and lower 26.9 per cent-owned Synthomer losses," she said in a note.
KLK's reported 9MFY26 results were hit by an RM1.62 billion non-cash impairment on its 27 per cent-owned Synthomer stake, resulting in a net loss of RM668 million.
Ng viewed the impairment as largely valuation-neutral, as CIMB Securities' sum-of-the-parts valuation already marks Synthomer to market.
The write-down, she said, also materially reduces the risk of further sizeable impairment charges while having no cash flow impact or effect on KLK's dividend prospects.
Operationally, plantation Ebit rose eight per cent year-on-year in Q3 FY26 on higher FFB production, despite a four per cent decline in realised CPO prices to RM3,756 a tonne.
Manufacturing Ebit more than doubled to RM136 million, driven by stronger oleochemical contributions and lower non-oleochemical losses.
CIMB Securities lowered its FY26-FY27 earnings forecasts between one per cent and four per cent due to higher associate losses, partly offset by an RM50-a-tonne increase in its Malaysia CPO price assumptions to RM4,450 for 2026 and RM4,550 for 2027.
"We see FY27 as a potential earnings reset year, as the Synthomer write-down substantially reduces the risk of further sizeable impairments, while 24.3 per cent-owned MP Evans could contribute RM80–100 million annually to KLK's earnings.
"The restructuring of KLK's Indonesian funding arrangements should also reduce foreign exchange volatility," Ng added.
CIMB Securities continues to view KLK as a laggard CPO play, with potential upside from new manufacturing capacity, higher-value speciality products and its sizeable land bank.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NationGate hits one-year high as investors look past earnings slump
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Shares of NationGate Holdings Bhd jumped nearly 15 per cent to a one-year high in early trade, as optimism over its optical networking business outweighed weaker quarterly earnings.
The electronics manufacturing services provider opened two per cent higher at RM1.52 from Monday's close of RM1.49 before climbing as much as 14.8 per cent to a morning high of RM1.71.
At 10.15am, the stock was trading at RM1.70, up 21 sen or 14.09 per cent, with more than 67 million shares changing hands. It was the most actively traded counter on Bursa Malaysia.
At that price, the company had a market capitalisation of RM3.87 billion. Year to date, the stock has gained nearly 87 per cent.
NationGate posted a sharp fall in second-quarter net profit, which dropped 79.1 per cent to RM10.90 million from a year earlier as lower contributions from its data computing business weighed on performance.
Despite the weaker earnings, UOB Kay Hian upgraded NationGate to "Buy" and raised its target price to RM1.88, based on 24 times its 2027 price-to-earnings ratio.
The target implies the stock could gain another 11 per cent from its current price over the next 12 months.
UOB Kay Hian said NationGate's first-half earnings came in below its expectations, but expects profitability to improve as the company's optical networking business moves beyond its initial gestation period.
It expects rising volumes to lift margins as the business scales up.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rantau Panjang ICQS sees fewer border movements amid Thai security concerns
Article:
PASIR MAS: Movement through the Rantau Panjang Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) Complex has dropped following bombings, shootings and arson attacks in three southern Thai provinces last Saturday.
Rantau Panjang Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) commander Siti Khadijah Hamzah said 3,298 entries into Malaysia were recorded from Saturday to Monday, compared with 2,969 exits.
She said incoming movements stood at 2,068 on Saturday before dropping to 1,230 over Sunday and Monday.
"Outgoing movements stood at 1,696 on Saturday before falling to 1,273 over Sunday and Monday," she told Bernama recently.
She said the decline was believed to be linked to the simultaneous attacks at 51 locations in Narathiwat, Pattani and Yala last Saturday.
A Bernama check at the Rantau Panjang ICQS found the area unusually quiet, with none of the congestion typically seen even during public holidays.
Previously, vehicles heading into Thailand would queue for almost a kilometre, while cross-border movements could reach 5,000 people on weekends and public holidays.
The decline is believed to have prompted some Malaysians to postpone trips to southern Thailand for tourism, shopping and family visits.
Narathiwat was previously placed under a curfew from 10.15pm to 5am following more than 50 incidents, including bombings, the burning of government offices and tyre-burning attacks, across the three provinces.
The explosions in Narathiwat also shook homes and caused anxiety among residents along the Malaysia-Thailand border, including those in Kampung Lubok Gong and Kampung Tersang in Rantau Panjang.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Firefighters contain half of 51.4ha Pengerang peat fire
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: Firefighters have contained 25 hectares of a 51.4-hectare peat soil fire along Jalan Bypass Punggai-Sebana Cove here in Pengerang here, today.
Johor Fire and Rescue Department operation commander Muhammad Tarmizi Md Jaafar said firefighting and firebreak operations were progressing smoothly, with teams maintaining 24-hour surveillance of the affected area.
Drone units were also deployed to monitor the fire and track hotspots.
The 51.4-hectare area, equivalent to about 73 football fields,
caught fire on Aug 24.
Tarmizi said firefighting operations were being carried out using the direct attack technique, while firebreaks were being established to contain the spread.
"The hot, dry weather and strong winds were hampering efforts, while soft ground, narrow road shoulders and limited access to open water sources were further complicating operations," he said in a statement today.
Motorists using Jalan Bypass Punggai-Sebana Cove were advised to drive cautiously due to poor visibility caused by thick smoke.
Meanwhile, the Air Pollutant Index (API) in Pengerang, particularly around Taman Bayu Damai and Punggai, reached the unhealthy level at 125.
Surrounding areas in Kota Tinggi also recorded unhealthy readings of 119.
Residents affected by the thick smoke were advised to wear face masks and remain indoors.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia's Destry Damayanti faces vetting for central bank's top job
Article:
JAKARTA: Lawmakers in Indonesia will on Wednesday conduct a "fit and proper" hearing for Destry Damayanti, the sole candidate nominated for its central bank governor, who could become the first woman to take the top job.
If given the green light, Destry, the current interim governor, would take charge at a tumultuous time in Indonesia, with concern lingering among businesses and investors about fiscal management, central bank autonomy, equity market transparency and the stewardship of the USUS$1.4 trillion G20 economy.
With parliament dominated by parties allied with President Prabowo Subianto, Deputy Governor Destry is widely expected to be confirmed by legislators, who have not ​rejected a sitting president's nominee for the post since 2008.
Reuters had reported Destry was the frontrunner for the job and the August 10 announcement of her candidacy gave a boost to the rupiah, which has plunged amid capital outflows triggered by anxiety and perceptions of policymaking uncertainty.
The rupiah is among Asia's worst-performing currencies, down about six per cent against the US dollar, while Indonesian stocks have fallen more than 25 per cent so far this year.
PREDECESSOR'S SURPRISE EXIT
Sentiment took a hit with the sudden resignation last month of central bank governor Perry Warjiyo midway through his second term, which followed the exit last year of long-time Finance Minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati, who was widely respected for her fiscal prudence.
Destry, 62, will be vetted by parliament's financial committee on Wednesday and needs to pass a plenary vote before being appointed by the president.
It is not clear whether the new governor would be appointed for a full five-year ​term or the remainder of Warjiyo's tenure, which expires in 2028.
Economists have said the Cornell-educated Destry, a senior Bank Indonesia deputy governor since 2019, would bring continuity to central bank policy and would prioritise stability while maintaining a good working relationship with the Prabowo administration.
At her first meeting as interim governor last week, the central bank held rates steady, prioritising rupiah stability while pledging to deploy other tools to support growth. Analysts said the policy tone was unchanged from that of Warjiyo.
The central bank has raised interest rates by 100 basis points since May to support the rupiah, including its first off-cycle benchmark rate hike in eight years in June.
Destry was an economist before working at Citibank and state-owned lender Bank Mandiri. She holds a master's from Cornell University and was a commissioner at Indonesia's deposit insurance agency between 2015 and 2019 before joining the central bank.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Japan's corporate services inflation accelerates in July
Article:
TOKYO: A key gauge of Japan's service-sector inflation rose 3.6 per cent in July from a year earlier, data showed on Wednesday, reinforcing the central bank's view that a tight labour market is pushing firms to pass rising costs on to consumers.
The increase in the services producer price index, which tracks the prices companies charge each other for services, followed a revised 3.4 per cent gain in June, Bank of Japan data showed.
The data added to signs of broadening inflationary pressure in the economy that have bolstered the case for a near-term interest rate hike.
Japan's core consumer inflation accelerated in July from a year earlier as firms passed on rising import costs from a weak yen and the US-Israeli war with Iran.
Sources have told Reuters the BOJ is set to raise the rate as soon as September and is considering hiking more aggressively thereafter from the current pace of roughly two times a year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Japan to support alternative Mideast oil pipelines
Article:
TOKYO: Japan plans to provide support for alternative pipelines in the Middle East as it seeks to improve energy security in the wake of the Iran war, local media reported Wednesday.
Before the conflict began in February, the world's fourth-biggest economy was heavily reliant on oil imports passing through the now-strangled Strait of Hormuz.
The Nikkei daily reported that Japan will assist initiatives by Saudi Arabia and other countries to expand and build new routes for crude which bypass the waterway.
Japan has already tapped its oil reserves to help cope with supply problems and increased crude imports from other countries including the United States.
Other measures to be decided by a government meeting later Wednesday include an initiative for a special crude oil reserve to produce naphtha, broadcaster NHK reported.
Naphtha is an oil by-product used in a wide range of industries.
The government is also expected to call "for maximising the use of nuclear power", NHK said, and provide support for next-generation perovskite solar cells.
Partly to meet a projected increase in power demand from AI, Japan has already been moving to revive its nuclear power sector, 15 years after the Fukushima disaster.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dollar moves in a narrow range ahead of inflation data, Jackson Hole
Article:
SINGAPORE: The dollar was rangebound in early Asian trading on Wednesday as an uneasy calm hung over currency markets, with investors awaiting inflation reports from major economies including the US ahead of the Jackson Hole symposium this weekend.
The greenback remained pinned in the narrow trading range it has sat in for the past week against most of its major peers ahead of the release of PCE data for July later on Wednesday.
"Signs of Middle East de-escalation, including plans to return US diplomatic staff to the region and efforts to reopen the Strait between Iran and Oman, weighed on oil prices and supported broader risk sentiment," Westpac analysts wrote in a note.
The US dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, snapped a three-day winning streak on Tuesday, and was holding steady at 98.918 in early Asian trading.
Oil prices slid in the Asian day on Wednesday, with Brent crude down 2.1 per cent at US$86.68, as Iran said it had restarted talks with neighbour Oman to manage the Strait of Hormuz and diplomatic negotiations between Washington and Tehran remained stalled.
The Australian dollar was up 0.1 per cent at US$0.7172 after the release of data showing the trimmed mean CPI inflation measure rose at an annualised rate of 3.6 per cent. Its kiwi counterpart was down 0.2 per cent at US$0.5962 ahead of an interest rate decision from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand next Wednesday.
The market overwhelmingly expects the central bank to hike interest rates by 25 basis points to 2.75 per cent, according to LSEG data.
However, the US dollar weakened 0.1 per cent against the Canadian dollar to CUS$1.38405 per dollar, retracing some of its gains against the loonie over the past two days after Ottawa hit back on Tuesday with retaliatory tariffs on about US$20 billion worth of US annual imports and rolled out aid for businesses and workers, after trade talks with Washington collapsed last week.
YEN STEADY
The euro was flat at US$1.1675, while the British pound was also unchanged at US$1.3647. The yen was steady at 159.14 yen, remaining firmly below levels that triggered joint intervention by US and Japanese officials in the past month.
Influential currency investor Stephen Jen said that the move marked a "watershed moment" for the currency. The central bank said on Wednesday that Governor Kazuo Ueda will not attend the US Federal Reserve's annual Jackson Hole gathering this week due to a schedule conflict.
Bank of Japan board member Naoki Tamura will attend on his behalf. A majority of economists in a Reuters poll said the Bank of Japan will likely move more swiftly than previously expected and raise interest rates again in September, with the terminal rate also likely to be higher.
Cryptocurrencies continued to roar back to life as investors revived dollar debasement trades. Bitcoin was up 0.8 per cent at US$78,829.03, while ether was up 0.7 per cent at US$2,453.10. So far this month, they are up 25 per cent and 31 per cent, respectively. However, gold slipped 0.5 per cent to US$4,633.94, paring its monthly gains to 15 per cent.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dashcam footage surfaces of alleged fatal Shah Alam group fight
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR : A dashcam recording believed to have captured part of a violent attack in Section 28, Shah Alam, which left one man dead and another seriously injured yesterday, has surfaced.
The recording, taken from a vehicle passing the scene at the time of the incident, appears to show two victims on the road as several men and vehicles converge at the location.
Although the footage is grainy due to the distance from which it was recorded, the scene is clear enough to show one of the victims sitting on the road, believed to be bleeding, while a blue Perodua Alza mounts the curb and stops near him before moving closer to the other victim.
Two men are then seen approaching the second victim.
At least two more men are seen getting out of the blue Alza and moving towards the second victim before the recording ends.
Yesterday, it was reported that police have arrested a man following a group fight at Jalan Mandolin 33/5, Taman Alam Megah, which resulted in the death of another man.
Shah Alam police chief Assistant Commissioner Sarudin Samah said police were alerted after a member of the public reported a
fight involving a group
of men.
"Preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred at 2pm. CCTV footage showed several men involved in a confrontation, during which slashing took place
"A car then struck one of the suspects, killing him at the scene," he said in a statement.
Police subsequently arrested a man in connection with the incident.
An investigation paper has been opened under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years and at least 12 strokes of the rotan upon conviction.
Those with information can contact investigating officer Assistant Superintendent Shamsiah Noor Zakaria at 012-830 8706, or the nearest police station.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kuching airport repairs underway after storm damages ceiling
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 26 — Repair works have been carried out at Kuching International Airport (KIA) following damage to part of its external ceiling structure caused by severe weather on Tuesday.
Malaysia Airports, in an update posted on its official Facebook page, said the affected area had been secured to allow the repair works to be carried out safely.
“Repair works at KIA are underway on the section of the external ceiling structure affected by the severe weather earlier today (Tuesday),” it said.
It added that airport operations were continuing as normal.
“We appreciate the patience and cooperation of passengers and airport users while these works are being completed,” Malaysia Airports said.
On Tuesday afternoon, a section of the roof at the arrival area of KIA was damaged following strong winds and heavy rain that swept through Kuching.
The incident was among several reports of weather-related damage in the city, including uprooted trees in various areas. — The Borneo Post

Title: Coroner walks out during Zara Qairina inquest after saying ‘Am I not fair enough?’ twice
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 26 — The Coroner’s Court hearing the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina Mahathir saw a tense moment today when Coroner Judge Amir Shah Amir Hassan suddenly stood and left his bench after twice asking, “Am I not fair enough?” during questioning of consultant psychiatrist Dr Wong Haw Huo.
The inquest was subsequently paused for about 50 minutes before resuming.
The exchange took place while Wong, the 75th witness in the inquest, was being questioned by lawyer Datuk Ram Singh, counsel for one of the teenagers charged in the bullying case involving Zara Qairina.
The lawyer had repeatedly asked Wong to provide direct answers to his questions, including on the cause of Zara Qairina’s fall and whether the teenager was alone before the incident.
Datuk Rizwandean M. Borhan, representing Zara Qairina’s mother, then remarked that Ram’s questioning of Wong appeared harsh.
Ram then responded: “Sir, don’t use the word harsh on me. In the past and towards the end, they (other counsels) were also very harsh, but this is very important for us. Very important.”
Judge Amir Shah then said: “But this is an inquest, not a trial.”
Ram responded: “I’m not saying it’s a trial, Sir. I mean let’s be fair to us. Let’s be fair.”
Judge Amir Shah then asked: “Am I not fair? Am I not fair enough?”
Ram replied: “You are fair, Sir,” prompting the coroner to repeat: “Am I not fair enough?”
Ram then said: “No, Sir. Let’s not get agitated with this. He (Wong) is going round and round and explaining.”
After the 50-minute pause, Ram apologised to the court, saying he had not intended his earlier remarks to be construed as questioning the fairness of the proceedings.
Ram also said the coroner’s decision to leave the courtroom had come as a shock to him as counsel in the inquest, adding that he hoped such an incident would not recur. Rizwandean also tendered an apology.
Judge Amir Shah accepted the apologies from Ram and Rizwandean, but reminded counsel to remain cautious and professional in conducting themselves throughout the inquest.
He also apologised, saying it was the first time in his 21 years of service that he had walked out from the bench.
“I should also apologise to you all for bursting out, and this is the first time that I walked out from the bench, with a little pain in my chest. Let’s not be emotional. Let’s be professional. That is the main aim for this inquest,” he said.
Moving on, Wong told the court that the last student to encounter Zara Qairina before the fall has been regarded as an important person in assessing the teenager’s mental state shortly before the incident.
Wong said interviewing the student would have enabled the psychiatrists to better understand Zara Qairina’s conversation, appearance, speech, behaviour and emotional condition at the time.
He said such information was important in establishing Zara Qairina’s mental state, including her understanding of the possible consequences of her actions.
Zara Qairina died at Queen Elizabeth Hospital on July 17, 2025, a day after she was found unconscious in a drain near her school hostel at about 4 am. — Bernama

Title: Look beyond racial and political lines this Merdeka, urges Sultan of Selangor
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 26 — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, has urged Malaysians to use this year’s National Day celebrations to reinforce national unity by looking past racial, religious, and political divides.
His Royal Highness made the call after officiating a flag-raising ceremony at Dataran Selangor on Wednesday. The event marked the start of the official flag-flying period, running until September 17 in conjunction with Merdeka Day and Malaysia Day..
The Sultan had earlier consented to the Jalur Gemilang being hoisted at the Selangor State Flagpole throughout the commemorative period.
“Although we differ in race, religion, language, political ideology and background, the Jalur Gemilang reminds us that we remain citizens of the same nation,” the Sultan said.
“This flag belongs to all of us. We must be proud because it is a symbol of national unity.”
The Sultan stressed that the spirit of Merdeka must go beyond ceremonial pageantry, calling on citizens to honour those who have dedicated their lives to bridging communal divides.
He also highlighted the importance of nurturing the younger generation with mutual respect and appreciation for diverse cultures, races, and faiths.
Directing his message to political leaders, the Sultan delivered a pointed reminder that national leaders shoulder a vital duty in safeguarding unity.
“Leaders and politicians must set an example by practising moderation, tolerance and compassion, and must not use political, racial or religious differences as a reason to divide the people,” he said.
The Sultan observed that while hoisting thousands of flags across the country during the independence month is straightforward, the true test lies in cultivating a nation where every Malaysian genuinely feels respected, valued, and proud of their citizenship.
He said that the Jalur Gemilang draws no distinction between ethnic communities, whether Malay, Chinese, Indian, Kadazan-Dusun, Iban, or others, nor does it discriminate across religious traditions including Islam, Buddhism, Christianity, and Hinduism.
“Independence is not merely something to be celebrated, and the flag is not merely something to be flown,” the Sultan said.
“Their true value lies in our collective ability to defend a nation whose people can live together in peace, mutual respect and unity.”

Title: WhatsApp ‘boss’ scam leaves Terengganu car dealership RM452,000 poorer
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 26 — A car dealership company suffered losses of RM452,000 after its clerk fell victim to a phone scam syndicate.
Kuala Terengganu district police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the 50-year-old finance clerk received a WhatsApp message last Monday from a suspect whom she believed to be the company owner.
He said the suspect instructed the victim to provide the company’s account balance and make three separate transfers totalling RM452,000 to three different accounts on the same day.
“The following day, the suspect instructed the victim to make an additional transfer of RM235,000 to another account.
“The victim, who became suspicious after receiving numerous transaction requests, contacted the company owner by phone to verify the matter, only to learn that her employer had not given such instructions,” he said.
Azli said the victim lodged a police report at 11.19 am yesterday after realising she had been duped, and the case was being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Penang SPM candidate targeted in sexual cyberbullying gets Education Dept support, protection
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 26 — The Penang State Education Department (JPNPP) has assured that necessary measures are in place to ensure the safety and wellbeing of an Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidate who was subjected to harassment through WhatsApp here.
Its director Mohamad Dziauddin Mat Saad said appropriate steps had been taken to protect the identity of the 17-year-old student and ensure that the incident did not disrupt her preparations for the SPM examination.
“The situation has now eased and the school will ensure that the student can attend classes without any disruption while providing her with the necessary support and guidance.
“We would like to assure parents that the school is taking steps to safeguard the student’s wellbeing,” he told reporters after assessing the school’s preparedness for haze at Sekolah Kebangsaan Sungai Gelugor here today.
He said a police report had also been lodged over the case, with investigations currently being conducted at the school and several locations linked to it.
Mohamad Dziauddin said the school had also advised the student to seek guidance and counselling to help her manage her emotions and focus on her SPM preparations.
He said JPNPP would continue to monitor the case and work with the school and parents to safeguard the student’s safety and wellbeing.
A mother, who wished to be identified only as Nur, 46, recently urged the authorities to expedite investigations into those allegedly responsible for repeatedly subjecting her 17-year-old daughter to sexual cyberbullying.
The woman said her second child, an SPM candidate, had experienced emotional distress after her face, name, class and phone number were allegedly circulated through obscene posters and fake social media accounts since April. — Bernama

Title: One China policy: Understanding Malaysia’s position on Beijing and Taipei
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s remarks on Taiwan have brought renewed attention to Malaysia’s One China policy and its relations with Beijing and Taipei.
In an August 2026 interview with
Al Jazeera
, the Pakatan Harapan chairman said: “I see Taiwan as part of China, period”.
When asked about Beijing’s refusal to rule out military force for reunification, Anwar drew a comparison with Malaysia, saying that if a Malaysian province attempted to break away, he would use force to protect national unity.
The remarks were welcomed by Beijing and criticised by Taipei.
Anwar later reiterated that Malaysia prefers a peaceful resolution and that its position under the One China policy remains unchanged since 1974.
What is the ‘One China’ framework?
There are two interpretations of the framework.
One is Beijing’s “One China Principle”, which asserts that there is only one China, that the People’s Republic of China (PRC) is its sole legal government, and that Taiwan is an “inalienable part” of Chinese territory. Beijing views cross-strait relations as an internal affair, according to news reports citing international relations analysts.
Malaysia’s “One China Policy”, meanwhile, was established through a 1974 Joint Communiqué that formally established diplomatic relations with Beijing, making Malaysia the first Asean country to do so. The communiqué was signed by then prime minister, the late Tun Abdul Razak, and his Chinese counterpart Zhou Enlai on May 31 that year.
The policy means that while Kuala Lumpur officially recognises the PRC as the sole legal government of China and acknowledges Beijing’s position on Taiwan, it does not formally endorse Beijing’s claims over the island.
Putrajaya’s One China policy also emphasises the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait.
Beijing and Taipei’s response
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian commended Anwar, saying his remarks reflected international consensus and supported Beijing’s position on Taiwan.
Taiwan’s Foreign Ministry rejected the remarks, saying Taiwan is not a province of China and expressing concern that such rhetoric could legitimise the use of military coercion. Taiwanese officials also warned the comments could affect investor confidence.
Will Anwar’s comments affect ties with Taiwan?
Malaysia has no official diplomatic ties with Taiwan, but both sides maintain robust unofficial economic, cultural and technological links.
The Malaysian Friendship and Trade Centre, Taipei (MFTC), established in 1987, serves as Malaysia’s representative office in Taipei, while Taiwan is represented by the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office in Kuala Lumpur. In the absence of formal diplomatic relations, the two offices perform many functions typically associated with embassies.
Whether Taipei will follow its statement with further action remains to be seen, while reactions in Taiwanese and Chinese media have been mixed.
Analysts have suggested Anwar’s remarks could dampen Taiwanese investor appetite if Malaysia is perceived as leaning more heavily towards Beijing, particularly as technology companies value geopolitical predictability.
A columnist in
China Times
noted that Taipei’s responses to similar statements by Southeast Asian countries have generally been limited to official rebuttals, arguing Taiwan is more likely to continue pursuing its “New Southbound Policy” to diversify its economic footprint away from mainland China.
In 2025, total trade between Malaysia and Taiwan reached US$54.49 billion, up from US$38.63 billion in 2024, according to a note on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ website.
Taiwan was Malaysia’s fourth-largest trading partner, accounting for 7.6 per cent of Malaysia’s total trade.

Title: Three more nabbed over illegal race on Malaysia-Singapore Second Link
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Police have arrested three more men in Kuala Lumpur over a brazen illegal street race that brought traffic to a halt along the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link.
Kulai police chief Tan Seng Lee said the latest arrests bring the total number of individuals detained in connection with the incident to 11,
Kosmo
reported.
The three suspects will be produced in court for a remand application.
“Further investigation into this case is ongoing under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987,” he said.
Police had earlier rounded up eight men on Sunday, including a motorsport influencer, obtaining a four-day remand order to facilitate investigations.
The incident unfolded at around 7am on Sunday along the stretch from KM33 (Senai Toll Exit) to KM31 (Johor Premium Outlets Exit).
A 30-second viral video sparked widespread public outrage after showing the group blocking morning motorists across the expressway to clear the route for the race.

Title: Bersatu leadership approves two Pahang reps’ move to back Umno menteri besar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Two Bersatu assemblymen in Pahang have thrown their support behind Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail of Umno, with the party's top leadership signalling its backing for the move.
Kuala Sentul assemblyman Datuk Jasri Jamaluddin and Lepar assemblyman Datuk Mohd Yazid Mohd Yunus — Bersatu's only two elected representatives in the 42-seat Pahang assembly — signed a memorandum of understanding with Wan Rosdy, pledging their backing for his administration until the next state election, expected by early 2028.
In a media statement issued the same day, Bersatu vice-president Datuk Seri Ahmad Faizal Azumu confirmed that the two ADUNs had informed the party leadership of their intention beforehand and left the final call to the party.
“The Bersatu political bureau, chaired by Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, president of Bersatu, discussed the matter from all angles and, in principle, supports the action.
“This decision was made to ensure political stability in the state of Pahang and to ensure that the welfare of the people in both of the respective constituencies receives due attention and representation from the Pahang state government,” Ahmad Faizal said.
Jasri and Yazid echoed this reasoning in their own joint statement, saying the understanding reached with the menteri besar would help ensure development and welfare priorities in Kuala Sentul and Lepar are not neglected.
They added that they would continue discharging their duties as elected representatives and cooperate with the state administration,
FMT
reported.
Wan Rosdy has headed the Pahang state government since a hung assembly emerged from the November 2022 state election. That election left Perikatan Nasional as the single largest bloc, edging out the ruling Barisan Nasional coalition by one seat, but Wan Rosdy was reappointed a week later at the helm of a BN–Pakatan Harapan coalition government.
Bersatu, as part of Perikatan Nasional, had held two of PN's seats in the assembly, alongside 15 from PAS.
With Jasri and Yazid's declared support, Wan Rosdy's administration now commands backing from 27 of the assembly's 42 seats.

Title: Penang Education Dept sets up haze ‘war room’, schools to switch to home learning once API hits 200
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 26 — The Penang Education Department (JPNPP) will implement home-based teaching and learning (PdPR) in schools if the Air Pollutant Index (API) due to haze reaches 200.
Its director Mohamad Dziauddin Mat Saad said the move was in line with guidelines set by the Ministry of Education (MOE) through the circular on school management during haze, which was drawn up jointly with the Ministry of Health (MOH) and the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma).
“JPNPP will closely monitor developments related to the haze and will not wait until the last minute to inform schools if there is a need to suspend school operations and implement PdPR,” he told reporters after assessing the haze preparedness level at Sekolah Kebangsaan Sungai Gelugor here today.
He said the department would assess API reading trends at four API monitoring stations in Penang, namely Minden, Balik Pulau, Seberang Jaya and Perai, at 6 pm or 8 pm the previous day to determine the necessary action for the following day.
He said JPNPP had set up a ‘war room’ on Aug 13 to monitor the haze situation in the state from time to time, including developments in API readings, before informing the district education offices (PPD) to relay the information to schools in stages.
Mohamad Dziauddin said parents need not worry as his department has a special team monitoring the haze situation, with priority given to the safety, health and comfort of the school community. He also advised schools and parents to remind students to make early preparations, especially those at risk of respiratory problems.
Meanwhile, he said JPNPP was preparing a contingency plan to deal with a possible deterioration in air quality due to the haze, which could affect the hosting of the Malaysia Schools Sports Council (MSSM) Football Championship and the 15th Malaysian Scout Jamboree (MYJAM15), scheduled to begin on Aug 28.
He said discussions had been held with the MOE’s Sports, Co-Curriculum and Arts Division (BSKK) regarding the preparations should weather conditions and API readings worsen.
“One of the options being considered is to adjust the football match schedule based on API readings. For example, if the API reading is lower in the morning, matches could be played at that time,” he said.
Regarding MYJAM15, Mohamad Dziauddin said the national scouting organisation is expected to discuss necessary early measures, in addition to having set up a special operations room to monitor and manage the haze situation throughout the programme.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is expected to officiate MYJAM15 on Aug 29, which will be attended by more than 5,000 local scouts and over 450 international scouts from 11 countries, including South Korea, Indonesia, Singapore and Sri Lanka. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia must move beyond reactive API readings to forecast haze, says air quality researcher
Article:
KUALA NERUS, Aug 26 — Malaysia should develop an early haze warning system to protect public health following recurring episodes of air pollution or haze.
Universiti Sultan Zainal Abidin (UniSZA) Besut Campus director Associate Professor Dr Azman Azid said it was time for Malaysia to shift its approach from crisis management to a more proactive crisis prevention strategy.
Azman, who is also a researcher in air quality and environmental issues, said most of the data required to develop an early haze warning system was already available and could be integrated to enable haze risks to be detected earlier, thereby reducing respiratory-related illnesses.
“While we focus on Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and the movement of smoke, there is a far more worrying development, namely the impact on public health. The Ministry of Health (MOH) reported that monitoring between the 32nd and 33rd epidemiological weeks showed a 259 per cent increase in asthma cases, from 61 to 219 cases.
“This signals that as the country faces deteriorating air quality, the burden of respiratory diseases is also recording a significant increase. Therefore, we need to change the way the country deals with haze, from an approach of monitoring, warning and acting to a proactive approach that includes forecasting, preventing, protecting and acting,” he said in a statement today.
Azman said Malaysia already had a weather forecasting system and that it was time for the country to have a haze forecasting system that was easy for the public to understand.
He added that a haze and health warning system could be developed by integrating hotspot data, satellite imagery, meteorological data, air trajectories, API readings, respiratory disease patterns and fine particulate matter measuring 2.5 micrometres in diameter (PM2.5).
He said hotspot data could indicate the location of fires, satellite imagery could identify smoke plumes, meteorological data could determine wind direction and speed, while atmospheric trajectory models could estimate the direction from which air masses originated and their movement.
He said if the model showed an increase in PM2.5 in a particular area within 48 to 72 hours, hospitals and clinics could raise their level of preparedness earlier, while schools could plan outdoor activities for students accordingly.
“Malaysia is also involved in regional cooperation through the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution. The question is not whether we have the data, but to what extent the data is truly integrated to enable haze to be forecast earlier.
“API is certainly important as it provides information on the current air quality, but from a risk management perspective, waiting for the API to rise before taking action means we are only acting after pollutants are already in the air. An early haze warning system does not need to replace the API, but rather complement it,” he said.
Azman said at the same time, authorities needed to be more firm in strengthening and enforcing laws related to open burning, bush fires and the monitoring of peatland areas in the country.
He said cooperation among Asean countries also needed to progress further, including in areas such as mapping fire sources, smoke trajectory forecasting, technology sharing, firefighting assistance and response mechanisms, rather than merely sharing data and taking action.
“In reality, air and smoke do not recognise national borders. Therefore, Asean cooperation needs to be strengthened so that action can be taken before pollution develops into a regional crisis.
“Technology, enforcement and diplomacy alone are not enough. Addressing haze requires a combination of fire prevention, peatland management, atmospheric modelling, regional cooperation and more sustainable land use.
“In the short term, we may not be able to prevent every plume of smoke from entering the country, but we can still reduce fires, forecast smoke movement earlier and, more importantly, protect public health,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Three dead after Perodua Viva skids and crashes on Kunak-Semporna road
Article:
KUNAK, Aug 26 — Three people were killed and three others injured after the car they were travelling in skidded and crashed at KM7 of Jalan Kunak-Semporna here yesterday.
Kunak police chief Supt Rejali Ak Angong said in the 6.03 pm incident, the driver and two passengers were pronounced dead at the scene by medical personnel from the Ministry of Health.
“In the incident, a Perodua Viva driven by a local man, together with five passengers comprising two adults and three children, was travelling from Kalabakan to their home in Kampung Sungai Langgas here.
“Upon reaching the location, the driver of the car lost control, and the vehicle skidded,” he said in a statement here today.
Rejali said the accident also left one passenger seriously injured and two others with minor injuries. They were sent to Kunak Hospital for further treatment.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Rejali also advised all road users to remain vigilant and considerate while driving. — Bernama

Title: One dead, three injured after 4WD crashes into tree at Miri public park
Article:
MIRI, Aug 26 — One person died while three others were injured after the four-wheel-drive (4WD) vehicle they were travelling in crashed into a tree at Taman Awam Miri, Jalan Bintulu-Miri, early this morning.
The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) said the 24-year-old man who died in the crash was trapped in the driver’s seat.
The department said it received an emergency call at 3 am, prompting fire and rescue personnel from the Miri Fire and Rescue Station to be dispatched to the scene, about four kilometres from the station.
“Firefighters managed to extricate the trapped victim using special equipment.
“The victim was later pronounced dead at the scene by a Ministry of Health (MOH) medical officer and the body was handed over to the police for further action,” Sarawak JBPM said in a statement today.
The department said one passenger suffered serious injuries while two others sustained minor injuries in the incident, and all three received initial treatment from MOH personnel at the scene.
The rescue operation ended at 3.53 am. — Bernama

Title: BMW driver dies after crashing into parked cars in Bukit Mertajam, two others hurt
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Aug 26 — A man was killed and two others, including a pedestrian, were injured in an accident involving three cars on Jalan Baru in Taman Pauh here early today.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis, in a statement today, said the department received a distress call about the crash at 2.31 am, before a team arrived at the scene nine minutes later.
He said the crash involved a BMW, a Perodua Myvi and a Proton Persona.
However, John said the Perodua Myvi and Proton Persona were stationary on the road shoulder when the incident occurred, while their drivers were not at the scene.
“Upon arrival at the scene, fire and rescue personnel found the BMW driver and a passenger trapped in the vehicle.
“Firefighters managed to extricate the two trapped men at 3.22 am using special equipment, but the BMW driver was pronounced dead at the scene by Health Ministry medical personnel,” he said.
John said the injured BMW passenger and pedestrian were given initial treatment by the Health Ministry medical team before being taken to Seberang Jaya Hospital for further treatment.
The victim’s body was also sent to the same hospital for further action. — Bernama

Title: Three die after Toyota Vios and Honda City collide on JB-Mersing road
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Aug 26 — Three people died after a two-vehicle crash at KM 80 of the Johor Bahru–Mersing Road on Monday evening, police said.
Kota Tinggi OCPD Supt Yusof Othman said in a statement that police received a report of the accident at around 5:25pm.
The collision involved a Toyota Vios, driven by a 21-year-old local man with a 20-year-old local woman as a passenger, and a Honda City driven by a 35-year-old local man.
All three occupants suffered severe head and body injuries and were pronounced dead at the scene by the attending medical assistant, according to the statement. Their bodies have been sent to the Forensic Unit at Kota Tinggi Hospital for further investigation.
Police said the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which carries a punishment of five to ten years' imprisonment, a fine of RM20,000 to RM50,000, and a minimum five-year driving disqualification upon conviction.
Investigations into the accident are ongoing. Police have appealed to members of the public with information on the crash to come forward to the Traffic Division at Kota Tinggi District Police Headquarters or any nearby police station.
The police chief also urged road users to remain vigilant and adhere to traffic laws to help ensure safety on the roads.

Title: Southern Thailand violence puts a damper on cross-border travel from Malaysia
Article:
PASIR MAS, Aug 26 — Movement in and out of the Rantau Panjang Immigration, Customs, Quarantine, and Security (ICQS) Complex here has dropped following the bomb explosions, shootings, and building arson incidents in three southern Thai provinces last Saturday.
Rantau Panjang Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) Commander Siti Khadijah Hamzah said that 3,298 movements entering Malaysia were recorded from Saturday to Monday, compared to 2,969 outgoing movements.
She said that the volume of incoming movement on Saturday stood at 2,068 before dropping to 1,230 on Sunday and Monday.
“Outgoing movements, meanwhile, were recorded at 1,696 on Saturday and decreased to 1,273 on Sunday and Monday,” she told Bernama recently.
According to her, the decline is believed to be linked to the simultaneous shooting, bombing, and building arson attacks that occurred at 51 locations across the provinces of Narathiwat, Pattani, and Yala last Saturday.
Meanwhile, a Bernama survey at the Rantau Panjang ICQS found the area quiet, without the usual traffic congestion typically seen even during public holidays.
Previously, vehicles entering Thailand would queue for nearly a kilometer, with total cross-border movements reaching 5,000 people during public holidays or weekends.
This situation is believed to have caused some Malaysians to postpone their trips to southern Thailand for tourism, shopping, and family visits.
Previously, Narathiwat province was placed under a curfew from 10:15 PM to 5:00 AM after more than 50 incidents – including bombings, the burning of local government offices, and tire burning – were reported across the three provinces.
The loud explosions originating from Narathiwat, southern Thailand, also shook homes and caused anxiety among residents along the Malaysia-Thailand border, including Kampung Lubok Gong and Kampung Tersang in Rantau Panjang, Pasir Mas, Kelantan. — Bernama

Title: Predawn blaze claims lives of father and nine-year-old son in Kuala Nerus
Article:
KUALA NERUS, Aug 26 — A father and his nine-year-old son were killed in a house fire in Kampung Tok Jembal, near here, early this morning.
Kuala Terengganu District Police Chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor, in a statement today, said police were alerted to a fire involving a semi-permanent two-storey house near Sekolah Kebangsaan Tok Jembal at about 4 am.
He said the operation to extinguish the fire and rescue the 40-year-old man and his son was carried out by 16 personnel from the Kuala Nerus and Kuala Terengganu Fire and Rescue Stations.
“A Fire and Rescue Tender (FRT) and a Compact Fire and Rescue Tender (CFRT) were also deployed for the operation,” he said.
Azli said the cause of the fire and the amount of losses incurred were still under investigation. — Bernama

Title: Sanusi to Ramkarpal: Come give Muslims a talk about not gambling
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor has taken aim at DAP lawmaker Ramkarpal Singh, pointedly inviting the MP to deliver a religious lecture to Muslims on the vices of gambling.
Sanusi's remarks followed comments from Ramkarpal, who urged the state government to focus on educating Muslims against gambling rather than seeking ways to bypass a Federal Court ruling on commercial gaming licences.
Addressing a briefing organized by the Kedah Information Secretariat on the legal hurdles facing the state's gambling ban, Sanusi reiterated that his administration will not abandon its push to eliminate gaming premises,
FMT
reported.
“We already have someone from DAP reminding us not to look for ways (to ban gambling in Kedah),” Sanusi said.
“Fine, we’ll invite him to give a talk later. Let DAP give a talk to Muslims telling them not to gamble.”
On August 12, the Federal Court dismissed the Kedah government's application for leave to appeal an appellate court decision that ruled the state had acted unconstitutionally in refusing to renew local business licences for lottery and pool betting operators.
Following the apex court defeat, Sanusi asserted that the ultimate decision to permit or halt gambling operations in the state now rests squarely with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who also holds the finance portfolio.
Sanusi warned that approving licences for gaming outlets would spark widespread public backlash in Kedah.
“So the ball is in the finance minister’s court,” he said.
At the same event, PAS central legal and human rights bureau chairman Wan Rohimi Wan Daud claimed that gaming operators are mounting a similar legal challenge against neighbouring Perlis over its ban on numbers forecast outlets.
Wan Rohimi, who is also the Melor assemblyman, noted that a group had recently initiated court proceedings to overturn the policy.
“What Kedah has gone through may spread to Perlis next. I was informed that in Perlis, this gambling group has already filed a new case.
“They want to challenge it like in Kedah, and then target other states,” he said.
Perlis Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah stated in June that the state government remains resolute in shutting down gaming operations, upholding a phased closure policy initiated by his predecessor, Shukri Ramli.
Perlis completed the total shutdown of gaming outlets earlier this year following the closure of its final betting outlet in Padang Besar in early March.

Title: Khairy seeks court order against MYNIC to uncover identity of ‘Corruption Watch’ author
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Former health minister Khairy Jamaluddin has launched legal action against national domain registry MYNIC Berhad in a bid to identify the owner of an online portal over an allegedly defamatory article.
The disclosure application filed in court seeks the identity and corporate details of the registered owner behind the focusmalaysia.my domain name, following the publication of an article on March 10 titled “10 reasons Why KJ isn’t PM material, Malaysians must carefully examine his past track record”,
NST
reported.
The article in question was published under the pseudonym “Corruption Watch”.
Through the pre-action discovery application, Khairy is requesting the registered owner’s identity card or company registration number, residential or business address, email, and contact number.
He is also seeking particulars of all administrative and technical contacts linked to the domain.
Additionally, the application requests registration documentation, including original creation and expiration dates, the accredited registrar involved, and historical logs of any ownership transfers.
According to court filings, Khairy said that the true identity of the author writing under the “Corruption Watch” pseudonym remains anonymous and cannot be determined without judicial intervention.
His legal team previously served a letter of demand to Focus Malaysia Sdn Bhd on March 13. However, the company denied owning or operating the website, stating that it had divested its entire business operations around 2018.
In an affidavit in reply, MYNIC confirmed that it holds the records of the domain’s registered owner, including contact particulars and administrative details.
The national registry stated it has no objection to handing over the information if directed by a court order.
MYNIC also verified that the entity registered as the domain owner on March 10, when the article was published, remains the current owner on record, with no transfer of ownership recorded between March 10 and June 18, when Khairy filed his application.
However, MYNIC opposed Khairy’s broader request for correspondence and communications between the registry, the registrant, and the accredited registrar, contending that such records are irrelevant to the planned defamation suit.
Emphasising that it is an innocent third party rather than the intended defendant, MYNIC is seeking an indemnity against any potential liabilities, costs, or claims arising from compliance with a disclosure order, alongside legal costs for the application.

Title: Haze persists across Malaysia as 17 stations record unhealthy air quality
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Malaysia's air quality crisis showed no signs of abating this morning, with the Department of Environment's (DoE) MyEQMS portal recording 17 monitoring stations nationwide in the "Unhealthy" tier as at 8.45am today, as the prolonged haze episode stretched into another week.
Sarawak and the Klang Valley once again registered the most severe pollution levels on the DoE's real-time index.
Sri Aman recorded the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading nationwide at 167, followed closely by IPD Serian at 166 and Samarahan at 162, cementing Sarawak's status as the epicentre of the current haze crisis.
Elsewhere, Nilai in Negeri Sembilan matched Samarahan at 162, while Cheras in Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya both posted readings of 159.
Klang Valley smothered
Six stations across Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, and Putrajaya breached the unhealthy threshold as at 8.45am, reflecting the dense smog enveloping the greater Klang Valley conurbation.
Shah Alam logged the highest level in Selangor at 158, matching readings in Johan Setia and Seremban in Negeri Sembilan. Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur registered 152, followed by Klang at 151, Banting at 144, and Petaling Jaya at 123.
Across the wider peninsula, poor air quality expanded beyond traditional hotspots. Tangkak in Johor recorded an API of 153, Bukit Rambai in Melaka stood at 143, Alor Gajah registered 128, and Taiping in Perak reached 108.
The persistent smog aligns with assessments from the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability, which attributes the widespread haze to prolonged dry spells linked to the El Niño phenomenon, suppressed rainfall, and rampant open burning both domestically and regionally.
In Sarawak, environmental authorities identified transboundary smoke alongside local peat and forest fires as the primary drivers of worsening air quality, with several stations inching toward the "Very Unhealthy" threshold of 201 in recent days.
Under national environmental standards, an API reading between 101 and 200 is officially classified as "Unhealthy".
Health authorities advise the public to limit strenuous outdoor exertion, while high-risk groups, including young children, expectant mothers, the elderly, and individuals with respiratory or cardiovascular conditions, should take added precautions and wear protective masks when outdoors.

Title: Penang police hunt missing Kafa teacher, 26, ahead of September wedding
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 26 — Police are actively conducting investigations and efforts to track down a male Kelas al-Quran and Fardu Ain (Kafa) teacher who was reported missing after leaving his home at an apartment in Sungai Ara near here last Saturday.
Southwest District Police Chief ACP Anuwal Ab Wahab said that the police are also examining any information being circulated regarding the case.
“Therefore, the public is advised not to make speculations or spread unverified information that could cause anxiety among the community,” he said in a statement last night.
He added that members of the public with information regarding the whereabouts of Mohamad Hijazi Zamry, 26, are urged to channel it directly to the police at 04-8662222 or any nearby police station.
Mohamad Hijazi stands at 155 centimetres (cm) tall, weighs 54 kilograms (kg), has a tuesian (langsat) complexion and black hair, and was last seen wearing an orange long-sleeved T-shirt and black long pants.
Meanwhile, the victim’s father, Zamri Saidin, 53, said Muhammad Hijazi was reported missing after leaving to perform the Isyak prayers at a surau near his home.
He said that the eldest of seven siblings had earlier performed the Maghrib prayers in congregation with him and his younger sibling before informing them that he wanted to perform the Isyak prayers at the nearby surau by riding a blue Yamaha LC motorcycle.
Zamri said Muhammad Hijazi was scheduled to solemnise his marriage this September 2 after being engaged for about a year, and all wedding preparations had already been made.
In a separate development, South Seberang Perai District Police Chief Supt Jay January Siowou stated that his department is tracking down Nik Nursyazwani Aishah Jefri Arwan Shah, 15, who was reported missing after allegedly leaving her home in Nibong Tebal since yesterday and failing to return until today.
“Members of the public who have information or have encountered the teenager can contact investigating officer Insp Nur Anis Syamimie Nasir at 016-9391927 or any nearby police station to channel information,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Penang schools told to stay on alert as haze worsens
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 26 — The Penang Education Department (JPNPP) has directed all District Education Offices (PPD) and schools in the state to step up preparedness for the care, welfare and safety of students and education personnel during haze conditions.
JPNPP said it is monitoring haze developments and Air Pollutant Index (API) readings across the state, while schools have been told to monitor the readings continuously and remain alert to the latest warnings.
“All outdoor activities must be stopped when the API reading exceeds 100, while schools must be closed immediately when the reading exceeds 200. If the API reading exceeds 500, teachers and members of the implementing group do not need to report to school, subject to the prevailing regulations,” it said in a statement last night.
JPNPP also instructed schools to ensure sufficient drinking water supplies, encourage students to drink enough water and reduce exposure to outdoor air.
It said special attention should be given to students with health problems or those showing symptoms of illness, while the use of face masks among students and school staff is encouraged where appropriate.
“Schools must also report developments and measures taken to the PPD and JPNPP to facilitate monitoring and coordination of action at the state level,” it said.
Minden, Seberang Perai and Balik Pulau were among 29 areas nationwide that recorded unhealthy API readings as of 2 pm today, according to the Department of Environment (DOE). — Bernama

Title: Celebrity preacher, NGO secretary face charges over alleged RM12m misappropriation in Seremban court
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will charge the chairman of a non-governmental organisation (NGO), who is also a celebrity preacher, at the Seremban Sessions Court today in connection with the alleged misappropriation of funds worth more than RM12 million.
According to a press invite sent by the agency yesterday, the celebrity preacher and the NGO’s secretary, both in their 30s, will be charged at 9 am.
On April 22, the Negeri Sembilan MACC was reported to have arrested a freelance preacher suspected of abusing his position and misappropriating about RM12.3 million in funds from an NGO for personal gain.
Following investigations, Negeri Sembilan MACC froze 15 accounts, comprising three personal accounts, three NGO accounts and nine company accounts, with a total value of about RM16.5 million.
In addition, the MACC seized RM6,576 in cash, as well as foreign currency amounting to SAR95,568 and SGD795.
Also seized were three watches worth about RM5,000; three handbags (RM3,000); five bracelets (RM26,000); a ring (RM2,000); a necklace (RM7,000); and 51 one-gram gold pieces worth about RM31,000. — Bernama

Title: Police nab one suspect after man dies in Shah Alam brawl
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 26 — Police have arrested a man to assist in investigations into a fight involving several individuals in Taman Alam Megah here, believed to have occurred recently.
Shah Alam District Police Chief ACP Sarudin Samah said the suspect was arrested following information received from the public regarding a fight involving a group of men in the area.
“A review of closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage showed a group of men engaged in a fight, with several of them seen slashing one another.
“A blue multi-purpose vehicle was also seen striking one of the suspects, who died at the scene,” he said in a statement.
Earlier, a one-minute video dated Aug 23, 2026, went viral on social media showing a group of individuals fighting on the road before one of them was struck by a vehicle.
Sarudin said police had opened an investigation paper under Section 302 of the Penal Code and urged anyone with information to contact senior investigating officer ASP Shamsiah Noor Zakaria at 012-8308706 or the nearest police station.
He also urged the public to refrain from speculating about the incident. — Bernama

Title: Buying strata? New housing policy proposes showing long-term maintenance costs upfront, tighter management rules
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Buying a strata property could eventually involve more than knowing the purchase price, monthly instalment and maintenance fee.
With the recently launched National Housing Policy or Dasar Perumahan Negara (DRN) 2026-2035, the government proposes factoring longer-term maintenance and replacement costs into sale and purchase agreements for strata housing.
It is among several measures in the DRN aimed at improving the long-term maintenance and management of housing, including better maintenance planning, professional building management and amendments to the Strata Management Act 2013 (Act 757).
The policy takes a life-cycle approach to housing, meaning the focus is not only on constructing and selling a property but also on how much it will cost to operate, maintain and eventually replace components of a building over its useful life.
Firstly, what are strata and non-strata properties?
A strata property is one where ownership is divided into individual parcels or units, while areas and facilities such as lifts, corridors, swimming pools, landscaping and other shared facilities are treated as common property.
Condominiums and apartments are the most familiar examples, although certain landed developments can also be strata schemes.
Owners therefore have rights and responsibilities relating to both their individual parcel and common property, which is why they pay maintenance charges and contribute to a sinking fund.
A strata property is individually owned but shares common facilities and maintenance costs with other owners. — File picture by Hari Anggara
A non-strata property, such as a conventional landed house with its own individual title, generally does not operate under the same shared management structure.
This distinction matters because the condition of common facilities can affect the cost and value of a strata property even though they are outside the individual unit.
Maintenance and replacement costs
One of the DRN’s specific proposals is to amend sale and purchase agreements for strata housing to include estimated maintenance charges and replacement costs throughout the property’s life cycle.
The policy would give buyers a clearer picture of the longer-term cost of owning a property, beyond its purchase price and recurring maintenance charges.
Life Cycle Costing
The DRN proposes the use of Life Cycle Costing (LCC) for the design and maintenance of public housing, referring to the LCCsoft (software) application developed by the Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB) and the JKR Life Cycle Costing manual.
Life-cycle costing considers the total cost of an asset over its useful life, including operation, maintenance and future replacement.
The DRN also proposes guidelines for housing maintenance and facility management.
Strata management and maintenance costs
The policy proposes a performance assessment approach for strata management, including how maintenance costs are managed.
Rather than focusing only on whether maintenance fees are low, the approach would consider whether spending is adequate and sustainable given the age, design, facilities and condition of a development.
JMBs, MCs and strata management
The DRN is looking to strengthen the capacity and understanding of Joint Management Bodies (JMBs) and Management Corporations (MCs).
Under the existing framework, the Strata Management Act governs strata management, while the Strata Titles Act 1985 (Act 318) covers strata ownership.
A JMB operates during the joint-management period, while an MC comes into existence when the strata register is opened.
The government also plans to amend the Strata Management Act as part of the policy, with the changes intended to keep pace with the changing needs of strata management.
Professional management
The policy proposes increasing the number of professional building and property managers, alongside training for officials involved in property, planning and housing management.
The aim is to strengthen professional capacity in managing increasingly complex strata developments, including common facilities, maintenance, finances and insurance.
Building condition and urban renewal
The DRN requires dilapidation reports for residential buildings identified for urban renewal and building condition reports for public-housing maintenance.
Such reports could help determine whether a building requires maintenance, rehabilitation or redevelopment.
It wants to improve urban renewal guidelines, cost-benefit analyses (CBA) for redevelopment projects and greater protection and participation of existing communities.
For older strata schemes, this could provide a more structured basis for deciding whether a building should be maintained, rehabilitated or redeveloped.
Universal design
The DRN wants compliance with Universal Design Guidelines in all new housing developments.
Universal design aims to make buildings usable by a wider range of people, including older residents and persons with disabilities.
The policy complements measures such as grants to modify existing homes for senior citizens and persons with disabilities.
What this means for strata owners
For prospective buyers, the most significant proposal is the inclusion of estimated maintenance and replacement costs over the property’s life cycle in the sale and purchase agreement.
For existing owners, the focus is on stronger JMB and MC management, professionalisation and amendments to the Strata Management Act.
As for older developments, building-condition assessments, life-cycle costing and cost-benefit analyses could play a greater role in decisions on maintenance, rehabilitation or redevelopment.
The bigger picture
The DRN points towards a shift from managing strata buildings around their immediate maintenance needs to managing them according to their entire life cycle.
For strata owners, the question could eventually become not simply “how much is my maintenance fee”, but “what will it cost to maintain this building over its useful life”.

Title: MyKad printing services nationwide to face temporary disruption from tomorrow to Aug 31
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 25 — MyKad printing services nationwide are expected to experience temporary disruption starting tomorrow (Aug 26) until Aug 31 following the transition process to the new generation MyKad.
The National Registration Department (JPN) said it was currently implementing the transition from the existing MyKad structure to the new generation identity card.
Members of the public without urgent needs have been advised to temporarily postpone replacing or exchanging their MyKad during the period.
“For first-time MyKad applications for 12-year-old children, parents or guardians are also encouraged to wait a while to enable their children to receive the new generation MyKad when production begins in the near future,” JPN said in a statement today.
The department said it appreciated the public’s patience and cooperation throughout the transition process and apologised for any inconvenience that might arise. — Bernama

Title: Jeffrey Cheah says metal fatigue possible cause of Sunway Lagoon roller coaster incident
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Sunway Group founder Tan Sri Jeffrey Cheah has reportedly confirmed a roller coaster accident that injured 10 people occurred at Sunway Lagoon on Saturday.
The
New Straits Times
reported Cheah as saying authorities were investigating the incident, while he believed metal fatigue may have been a possible cause.
“It’s an incident that all of us regret very much. We are lucky that there were no fatalities,” Cheah was quoted as saying.
Subang Jaya district police chief ACP Wan Azlan Wan Mamat previously said 22 people, comprising Malaysians and foreign tourists aged between 11 and 44, were on the ride when the incident occurred at about 9pm on Saturday.
He said those injured were taken to medical centres in the Subang Jaya district for treatment, with all reported to have sustained minor injuries.
Police said a report was lodged at 11.45am the following day and investigations are ongoing.

Title: Sunway Lagoon says cooperating with authorities after roller coaster incident
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Sunway Theme Parks says that it is currently working closely and fully cooperating with all relevant authorities as they conduct a thorough investigation into the incident involving an attraction at Sunway Lagoon on Saturday, which affected 10 guests.
Confirming the incident, the company also expressed deep regret, saying that their thoughts are with the guests and their families.
“The safety and well-being of our guests are our highest priority. Since the incident, our immediate focus has been on the care, medical needs and well-being of those affected.
“We have provided the necessary medical assistance and support, and remain in close contact with the guests and their families,” the company said in a statement today.
Sunway Theme Parks said it would also continue to provide its full assistance to the authorities and support to those who were affected.
“Sunway Theme Parks takes this matter extremely seriously. We remain firmly committed to maintaining the highest standards of safety across our attractions and facilities,” it added.
Yesterday, Subang Jaya District Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Wan Azlan Wan Mamat was reported to have said that 10 people had sustained minor injuries in a roller coaster incident at a theme park.
The incident took place at about 9pm on Saturday, and the report was lodged with the police at 11.45am on Sunday. — Bernama

Title: Public toilets maintained, markets upgraded, drains improved: Housing Ministry says six initiatives surpass targets
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 25 — Six significant initiatives implemented by the Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) under Budget 2026 have exceeded their targets as of July 31, with the maintenance of public toilets in local authority (PBT) areas recording the strongest performance at 734 per cent, said Minister Nga Kor Ming.
He said the achievement reflected KPKT’s ability to implement the Madani Government agenda efficiently and responsively, particularly in providing better, more comfortable and inclusive public facilities.
“This achievement demonstrates that every ringgit allocated by the Government is being translated into tangible results that directly benefit the people.
“We do not want the allocation to remain just a figure on paper. Instead, it must translate into projects that can be seen, felt and enjoyed by the people,” he said in a statement today.
He said KPKT had successfully implemented nearly 16,000 public facility projects since the Madani Government took office in 2023, in addition to receiving prestigious accolades such as the National Development Award and the Prime Minister’s Innovation Award.
He said the public toilet maintenance initiative in PBT areas, which received an allocation of RM30 million, recorded the strongest performance at 734 per cent, with 367 projects successfully implemented compared with the original target of 50 projects.
Nga said the construction of Madani stalls and upgrading of dilapidated public markets recorded an achievement rate of 170 per cent, with 102 projects implemented compared with the target of 60 projects, involving an allocation of RM60 million.
In addition, he said 304 maintenance projects for non-Muslim places of worship were implemented compared with the initial target of 200 projects, recording an achievement rate of 152 per cent through an allocation of RM50 million.
Nga said the initiative to upgrade drainage and sewerage systems recorded an achievement rate of 102.67 per cent, with 154 projects implemented compared with the target of 150 projects, involving an allocation of RM55 million.
“This measure is part of KPKT’s ongoing efforts to strengthen basic infrastructure and improve drainage capacity, particularly to reduce the risk of disruptions and flash floods in PBT areas,” he said.
Meanwhile, Nga said all 113 projects to upgrade fire stations and fire department quarters had been successfully completed, with an allocation of RM10 million.
He said 57 out of the 64 programmes under the Bomba Bersama Rakyat Programme had been implemented as of July 31, achieving an implementation rate of 89 per cent.
“KPKT is committed to ensuring that the remaining programmes are fully implemented to achieve or exceed the 100 per cent target by the end of this year.
“This is in line with efforts to strengthen ties between the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) and the community, as well as increase public awareness of fire safety and prevention,” he said.
Nga said the achievement also reflected the effectiveness of cooperation among ministries, departments, agencies, local authorities, industry partners and the community in ensuring the Malaysia Madani development agenda was implemented comprehensively.
He also said KPKT would continue to strengthen its service delivery, with a focus on performance, results and impact on the people, to ensure every planned initiative was implemented efficiently and effectively. — Bernama

Title: Strong winds, heavy rain damage Kuching International Airport roof (VIDEO)
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 25 — A section of the roof at the arrival area of Kuching International Airport (KIA) was damaged by strong winds and heavy rain today afternoon.
Airport personnel were at the scene to assess the situation, while personnel from the People’s Volunteer Corps (Rela) were conducting traffic control.
The section of roofing which collapsed due to strong winds on Aug 25, 2026 at Kuching International Airport. — Photo by Shahrul Tready
Similar weather conditions were reported in other parts of Kuching, including an uprooted tree at Jalan BDC.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in an update issued at 3.55pm, forecast heavy rain and thunderstorms in most parts of Sarawak until 7pm.
The affected areas include Limbang, Miri (Marudi, Telang Usan, Bario and Beluru), Bintulu, Kapit (Kapit, Song and Bukit Mabong), Sarikei (Julau and Pakan), Sibu, Kuching (Kuching), Serian, Samarahan, Sri Aman (Lingga, Pantu and Sri Aman), Betong (Pusa) and Mukah (Mukah). — The Borneo Post

Title: MetMalaysia: Weak 3.1-magnitude earthquake strikes off Batu Pahat
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 25 — A weak earthquake measuring 3.1 magnitude struck the waters off Batu Pahat, Johor, at 4.12pm today.
In a statement, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the epicentre was located at coordinates 1.7 degrees north and 102.8 degrees east, about 18 kilometres (km) south-west of Batu Pahat.
“The quake was recorded at a depth of 10km.
“There is no tsunami threat to Malaysia,” it said in the statement issued today by the National Weather and Earthquake Operations Centre, MetMalaysia. — Bernama
